subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this experimental core `claws status` and destructive `claws remove` lifecycle slice as part of the RFC stack, rather than keeping removal ownership in narrower package or plugin surfaces?
rationale: The patch creates a new user-facing core lifecycle contract whose cleanup semantics span configuration, files, session state, and package owners; code review cannot decide whether that product boundary should be accepted.

options.title: Sponsor the experimental lifecycle slice
options.body: Keep the scope in the RFC stack, require exact-head proof of all referenced-resource cleanup modes, and review it together with the prerequisite package-lifecycle PR.

options.title: Narrow the core contract
options.body: Retain status and conservative release behavior in core, while moving optional or destructive package cleanup behind narrower owner-plugin or package lifecycle surfaces.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Defer the feature until maintainers settle the desired ownership and recovery model for Claw lifecycle removal.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the experimental lifecycle slice
recommendation.body: Keep the scope in the RFC stack, require exact-head proof of all referenced-resource cleanup modes, and review it together with the prerequisite package-lifecycle PR.
